title: Board-pattern readiness test — most-repeated question types
chapter: CBSE Class 10 Mathematics · Chapter 14 Probability (NCERT reprint 2026-27)
tagline: Practice questions modelled on past CBSE papers; not predictions of this year's paper.
disclaimer: Original questions modelled on question types that have repeated in CBSE board papers 2023-2026 and the Sample Question Papers 2024-25 to 2026-27. They are practice for readiness, not predictions of what will appear in any exam.
instructions: 40 questions. MCQ and assertion-reason: choose one option. Numeric: type a whole number. No calculator.

patterns.T1: Range of P(E); sure and impossible events
patterns.T6: Numbers or letters drawn at random
patterns.T7: Find a count from a given probability

S1.name: Classical definition, sure and impossible events
S1.tip: P(E) = favourable ÷ all outcomes; 0 ≤ P(E) ≤ 1; impossible 0, sure 1.

S2.name: Complementary events
S2.tip: P(not E) = 1 − P(E). 'Neither … nor': count what is left.

S3.name: A pack of 52 cards
S3.tip: 52 = 4 suits × 13; 12 face cards; 4 aces. 'A or B': subtract the overlap. Cards removed: recount the total.

S5.name: Two dice: sums and differences
S5.tip: Two dice: 36 outcomes, (1, 4) ≠ (4, 1). The 11 sums are not equally likely.

S6.name: Two dice: products and both-dice conditions
S6.tip: Both dice with a condition: multiply the choices (3 × 3 = 9). x > y: (36 − 6) ÷ 2 = 15.

S7.name: Numbers and letters drawn at random
S7.tip: Numbers from a to b: b − a + 1. 'Square or cube': add, then subtract the ones that are both.

S8.name: Finding a count from a given probability
S8.tip: Given P and the total: count = P × total.

S9.name: Case studies and traps
S9.tip: Read who accepts what (Example 12). Leap year: 52 weeks + 2 days → 2/7.

questions.question: Which of these can NOT be the probability of an event?
questions.explanation: A probability lies from 0 to 1; 7/6 > 1 (a 2023/2026 board type).

questions.question: A die is thrown once. The probability of getting a number less than 3 is:
The probability of a sure event is:
A die is thrown once. The probability of getting a prime number is:
A die is thrown once. The probability of getting a number greater than 6 is:
questions.explanation: No face shows more than 6: impossible event.

questions.question: If P(E) = 0.35, then P(not E) is:
A batsman hits a boundary 6 times in the 48 balls he plays. The probability that he does not hit a boundary on a ball is:
A bag has 4 red, 6 white and 5 black balls. The probability that a ball drawn at random is neither red nor white is:
questions.explanation: Neither red nor white = black: 5/15 (a 2024 board type, new numbers).

questions.question: The probability of guessing the correct answer to a question is x/12. If the probability of not guessing it is 2/3, find x.
Choose the correct option.
questions.explanation: Both true and R gives A.
questions.reason: For any event E, P(E) + P(not E) = 1.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

questions.question: How many face cards are there in a pack of 52 playing cards?
questions.explanation: King, queen and jack in each of 4 suits.

questions.question: One card is drawn from a pack of 52. The probability that it is a black king is:
One card is drawn from a pack of 52. The probability that it is a red card that is not a face card is:
One card is drawn from a pack of 52. The probability that it is a diamond or a jack is:
questions.explanation: 13 diamonds + 3 other jacks = 16 → 16/52 (a 2025 board type, new suit).

questions.question: The 4 aces are removed from a pack of 52 cards. One card is drawn from the rest. The probability that it is a face card is:
3 hearts and 5 clubs are missing from a pack of 52 cards. One card is drawn from the rest. The probability that it is a spade is:
questions.explanation: 52 − 8 = 44, all 13 spades remain (SQP 2026-27 Q18 type, new numbers).

questions.question: Cards numbered 3 to 52 are in a box. The probability that a card drawn at random shows a perfect square is:
questions.remediation: Video part 7: count a to b as b − a + 1.

questions.question: How many whole numbers are there from 15 to 84, both included?
Discs numbered 2 to 101 are in a box. The probability that a disc drawn at random shows a perfect square or a perfect cube is:
questions.explanation: 100 discs; 9 squares (4 to 100) + 3 cubes (8, 27, 64) − 1 (64) = 11 (SQP 2026-27 Q9 type, new numbers).

questions.question: A bag has 30 balls. The probability of drawing a blue ball is 2/5. How many blue balls are there?
A bag has 6 red balls and n blue balls. Drawing a blue ball is twice as likely as drawing a red ball. Find n.
The probability that a bulb from a lot of 500 is defective is 0.04. How many bulbs in the lot are not defective?

Case study: a carton has 80 shirts: 64 good, 10 with minor defects and 6 with major defects. A trader rejects only shirts with major defects. The probability that a shirt drawn at random is acceptable to him is:
The probability that a non-leap year, chosen at random, has 53 Sundays is:
questions.remediation: Video part 8: count the extra days.
